title: v4 drafted from parent ledger D022/D024/D025/D026 cluster trigger
body: Three distinct supervisor frictions surfaced in this week's cross-repo dogfood (plan 004 F001+F002 + plan 010 F002 + SpinDine v2 dispatch). Per parent plan 2026-05-11-001 ledger D026, cluster threshold ≥3 reached. v4 sourced directly from those three D-entries + a fourth derivative (supervisor checkpointing is the structural fix that addresses the same orphaned-state class as D025 even when shlex isn't the cause). Drafted while signals are fresh; status: draft for operator review before lock.

title: goal_type:infra (consistent with v1/v2/v3)
body: Same framing as v1/v2/v3 plans — harness substrate, not user-facing feature. Avoids Goal Governance V1 objective_contract requirement at lock time.

title: F004 depends_on F003 because F003 enables clean failure records
body: F003 (shlex-safe) makes parse errors produce structured warnings instead of unhandled exceptions. F004 (checkpoint artifacts) then captures the residual failure modes — env errors, missing schemas, OSError. Ordering matters: if F004 lands first, the checkpoint would record shlex crashes verbatim, but the underlying volley would still die mid-run; F003 first means F004 only triages truly-unexpected failures.

title: Out of scope: tee buffering, iterN cost regression, automated retry-on-crash
body: Three deliberately-deferred concerns. (a) Tee buffering of dispatch logs is operator-side (operators can copy from the bash task output file); not a supervisor-side fix. (b) iterN cost regression (D019 in parent) is a single observation so far — defer to v5 if it clusters with other cost signals. (c) Automated retry-on-shlex-crash is a separate concern; F003+F004 deliver clean failure surfaces, retry policy is its own design conversation.
